'''Heinrich Magnus Manske''' (born 24{{nbsp}}May 1974) is a German [[biochemist]] who is a researcher on [[malaria]]. He is a senior staff scientist at the [[Wellcome Sanger Institute]] in [[Cambridge]], UK<ref name="googlescholar" /><ref name="dblp">{{DBLP|name=Magnus Manske}}</ref><ref name="scopus">{{Scopus|id=25723615000}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Daub |first1=J. |last2=Gardner |first2=P. P. |last3=Tate |first3=J. |last4=Ramsköld |first4=D. |last5=Manske |first5=M. |author-link5=Magnus Manske |last6=Scott |first6=W. G. |last7=Weinberg |first7=Z. |last8=Griffiths-Jones |first8=S. |last9=Bateman |first9=A. |year=2008 |title=The RNA WikiProject: Community annotation of RNA families |journal=RNA |volume=14 |issue=12 |pages=2462–2464 |doi=10.1261/rna.1200508 |pmc=2590952 |pmid=18945806}}</ref> and a [[software developer]] of one of the first versions of the [[MediaWiki]] software, which powers [[Wikipedia]] and a number of other [[wiki]]-based websites.

==Early life==
Magnus Manske was born on 24{{nbsp}}May 1974 in [[Cologne]], Germany. He studied biochemistry at the [[University of Cologne]] and graduated in 2006 with a [[PhD]]; his dissertation was on an open source tool for [[molecular biology]], [[GENtle (software)|GENtle]].<ref name="Magnus Manske-2006">{{Cite thesis |last=Magnus Manske |title=GENtle, a free multi-purpose molecular biology tool |access-date=27 March 2016 |degree=PhD |publisher=University of Cologne |url=https://kups.ub.uni-koeln.de/1907/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150407083730/https://kups.ub.uni-koeln.de/1907/ |archive-date=7 April 2015 |year=2006 |author-link=Magnus Manske |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Alastair Kerr |date=21 June 2011 |title=Desktop Sequence Analysis: software review |url=https://bioinformatics.knowledgeblog.org/2011/06/21/desktop-sequence-analysis-software-review/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180930230415/https://bioinformatics.knowledgeblog.org/2011/06/21/desktop-sequence-analysis-software-review/ |archive-date=30 September 2018 |access-date=4 June 2013 |website=Bioinformatics Knowledge Blog}}</ref>

==Career==
As a student, Manske was one of the first contributors to the Internet encyclopedia [[Nupedia]], the precursor to Wikipedia, and later wrote one of the first versions of the MediaWiki software that Wikipedia runs on.<ref name="Claudia Lehnen-2008">{{Cite news |last=Claudia Lehnen |date=2 February 2008 |title=Der Wikipedia-Pionier aus Köln |trans-title=The Wikipedia pioneer from Cologne |url=https://www.ksta.de/ratgeber/der-wikipedia-pionier-aus-koeln,15189524,13249760.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712191226/https://www.ksta.de/ratgeber/der-wikipedia-pionier-aus-koeln,15189524,13249760.html |archive-date=12 July 2015 |access-date=22 June 2013 |work=[[Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger]] |language=de}}</ref> Manske has worked in [[Cambridge]] with the [[Wellcome Sanger Institute]] since April 2007,<ref name="Manske-2012">{{Cite journal |last1=Manske |first1=M. |author-link1=Magnus Manske |last2=Miotto |first2=O. |last3=Campino |first3=S. |last4=Auburn |first4=S. |last5=Almagro-Garcia |first5=J. |last6=Maslen |first6=G. |last7=o'Brien |first7=J. |last8=Djimde |first8=A. |last9=Doumbo |first9=O. |last10=Zongo |first10=I. |last11=Ouedraogo |first11=J. In 2012, Manske was co-author of a paper published in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' that demonstrated new ways to identify areas where malaria parasites are evolving, and described techniques for mapping malarial drug resistance. The researchers developed a technique to extract the malaria parasite DNA directly from the blood, which minimizes errors in sequencing.<ref name="Manske-2012" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=26 June 2012 |title=DNA Research; Putting parasites on the world map |work=China Weekly News}}</ref>

==Development of MediaWiki==
As a student, Manske was one of the most active contributors to the [[Nupedia]] project,<ref name="SpiegelJansson">{{Cite news |last=Kurt Jansson |date=14 January 2011 |title=Zehn Jahre Wikipedia – Der kurze Sommer der Anarchie |url=https://einestages.spiegel.de/static/authoralbumbackground/19921/der_kurze_sommer_der_anarchie.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222103446/https://einestages.spiegel.de/static/authoralbumbackground/19921/der_kurze_sommer_der_anarchie.html |archive-date=22 February 2014 |access-date=25 June 2013 |work=[[Der Spiegel]]}}</ref> submitting content on biology topics<ref name="Claudia Lehnen-2008" /> and developing tools and extensions for Nupedia.<ref name="Anderson" /> Later, unhappy with the existing software's limitations,<ref name="SpiegelJansson" /> Manske developed one of the first versions of what later became [[MediaWiki]].<ref name="Anderson">{{Cite book |last=Jennifer Joline Anderson |url=https://archive.org/details/wikipediacompany0000ande/page/44 |title=Wikipedia: The Company and Its Founders |publisher=ABDO |year=2011 |isbn=978-1-61714-812-5 |page=[https://archive.org/details/wikipediacompany0000ande/page/44 44]}}</ref><ref name="Zeit">{{Cite news |last=Torsten Kleinz |date=16 December 2012 |title=Neues Werkzeug soll Anfänger zur Wikipedia locken |url=https://www.zeit.de/digital/internet/2011-12/visual-editor-testversion |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190810110950/https://www.zeit.de/digital/internet/2011-12/visual-editor-testversion |archive-date=10 August 2019 |access-date=25 June 2013 |work=[[Die Zeit]]}}</ref> His new version of the software was installed in 2002.<ref name="SpiegelJansson" />

The wiki software that was initially used for Wikipedia was called [[UseModWiki]] and was written in [[Perl (programming language)|Perl]]. With issues of scale starting to present themselves as Wikipedia grew, in the summer of 2001, Manske started work on a replacement for UseModWiki that would be database-backed and would contain "wikipedia-specific features".<ref name="Sumana">{{Cite book |last1=Sumana Harihareswara |title=The Architecture of Open Source Applications |last2=Guillaume Paumier |publisher=Kristian Hermansen |year=2012 |isbn=978-1-105-57181-7 |editor-last=Amy Brown |chapter=MediaWiki |access-date=27 March 2016 |editor-last2=Greg Wilson |chapter-url=https://www.aosabook.org/en/mediawiki.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130924202227/https://aosabook.org/en/mediawiki.html |archive-date=24 September 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref> On 25 January 2002, Manske released the first version of a [[MySQL]]-based [[PHP]] wiki engine, called ''Phase II''.<ref name="Kumar">{{Cite news |last=Rajeev Kumar |title=Wiki Installation and Customization |url=https://ir.inflibnet.ac.in/handle/1944/990 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150721004201/https://ir.inflibnet.ac.in/handle/1944/990 |archive-date=21 July 2015 |access-date=4 June 2013}}</ref> One innovation implemented by Manske in Phase II was the use of namespaces in order to separate different types of pages, such as the "Talk" or "User" namespace, which distinguished it from older wiki software which didn't have different namespaces.<ref name="Sumana" /> Phase II also introduced a number of other features which are still present, including file upload, watchlists, automatic signatures, and user contributions list.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=27 January 2002 |title=Wikipedia:PHP script new features |url=https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:PHP_script_new_features&oldid=691 |url-status=live |journal=Wikipedia |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200607184331/https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia%3APHP_script_new_features&oldid=691 |archive-date=7 June 2020 |access-date=27 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Magnus Manske |date=27 January 2002 |title=[Wikipedia-l] New features list |url=https://lists.wikimedia.org/pipermail/wikipedia-l/2002-January/001188.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151112214155/https://lists.wikimedia.org/pipermail/wikipedia-l/2002-January/001188.html |archive-date=12 November 2015 |access-date=4 June 2013}}</ref> Manske's re-write also made it easier to integrate photographs in Wikipedia articles, and created a new user group: administrators, empowered to [[Deletion of articles on Wikipedia|delete pages]] and block vandals.<ref name="SpiegelJansson" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Erik Möller |date=9 May 2003 |title=Das Wiki-Prinzip |url=https://www.heise.de/tp/artikel/14/14736/1.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160902025025/https://www.heise.de/tp/artikel/14/14736/1.html |archive-date=2 September 2016 |access-date=25 June 2013 |publisher=[[Heise Online]]}}</ref>

Manske was an adherent of open source and specifically, the [[GPL]] license, and his work on the early versions of MediaWiki was released under the GPL license.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=N. A. Polukarova |date=June 2007 |title=The concept of open editing from the copyright viewpoint |journal=Automatic Documentation and Mathematical Linguistics |volume=41 |issue=3 |pages=104–107 |doi=10.3103/S0005105507030053 |issn=1934-8371 |s2cid=6463839 |quote=In simpler words, while the developers of proprietary programs use their copyrights to deprive most of the users of most of their freedoms, GPL adherents, including above-mentioned Magnus Manske, use these privileges to guarantee these freedoms to users.}}</ref>

Manske's Phase II software encountered load issues as Wikipedia continued to grow, so [[Lee Daniel Crocker]] did another re-write, which led to phase III, which was used from June 2002 and from 2003 onwards was called "MediaWiki".<ref name="Kumar" /> The resultant [[MediaWiki]] software is now used as the core platform for both Wikipedia and many [[Wikimedia Foundation|Wikimedia]] sister projects, as well as in many organizations and institutions.

Manske continued to develop extensions for MediaWiki and tools used to build Wikipedia and its sister projects, including tools to map category membership, compute category intersections, and import images from [[Flickr]] to [[Commons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Magnus' toys'n'tools |url=https://toolserver.org/~magnus/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140510153920/https://toolserver.org/~magnus/ |archive-date=10 May 2014 |access-date=4 June 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Magnus' tools on wmflabs |url=https://tools.wmflabs.org/magnustools/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200514170047/https://tools.wmflabs.org/magnustools |archive-date=14 May 2020 |access-date=4 June 2013}}</ref><ref name="Tools">{{Cite web |title=Tools Directory |url=https://tools.wmflabs.org/hay/directory/#/author/Magnus%20Manske |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190201013552/https://tools.wmflabs.org/hay/directory/#/author/Magnus%20Manske |archive-date=1 February 2019 |access-date=31 January 2019 |publisher=Wikimedia Foundation}}</ref>

==Tools==
As well as working on MediaWiki itself, Manske has made tools that work with it such as "wiki shoot me" that identifies on a map photos that are needed to be taken and allow them to be uploaded or Reasonator that take the raw information from Wikidata and presents it as if it were a Wikipedia article.<ref name="Vrandečić Pintscher Krötzsch 2023 p. ">{{Cite conference |last1=Vrandečić |first1=Denny |last2=Pintscher |first2=Lydia |last3=Krötzsch |first3=Markus |date=30 April 2023 |title=Companion Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2023 |publisher=ACM |publication-place=New York, NY, USA |pages=615–624 |doi=10.1145/3543873.3585579 |isbn=978-1-4503-9419-2 |doi-access=free |chapter=Wikidata: The Making Of}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Manske is recognized as the creator of the first article in the German Wikipedia, which was on the [[polymerase chain reaction]], first written by him in 2001.<ref>{{Cite news |date=28 December 2009 |title=German Wikipedia reaches landmark millionth entry |url=https://www.dw.de/german-wikipedia-reaches-landmark-millionth-entry/a-5064273 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150606174513/https://www.dw.de/german-wikipedia-reaches-landmark-millionth-entry/a-5064273 |archive-date=6 June 2015 |access-date=25 June 2013 |work=Deutsche Welle}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=dpa/mos |date=28 December 2009 |title=Deutsche Wikipedia erreicht eine Million Einträge |url=https://www.welt.de/wirtschaft/webwelt/article5655970/Deutsche-Wikipedia-erreicht-eine-Million-Eintraege.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160825050245/https://www.welt.de/wirtschaft/webwelt/article5655970/Deutsche-Wikipedia-erreicht-eine-Million-Eintraege.html |archive-date=25 August 2016 |access-date=8 March 2017 |work=[[Die Zeit]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Achim Sawall |date=28 December 2009 |title=Deutschsprachige Wikipedia erreicht die Millionenmarke |url=https://www.golem.de/0912/72088.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521171040/https://www.golem.de/0912/72088.html |archive-date=21 May 2021 |access-date=25 June 2013 |publisher=golem.de}}</ref>

[[Jimmy Wales]] in 2002 named 25 January as [[Wikipedia:Magnus Manske Day|Magnus Manske day]] in honor of his contributions to Wikipedia, proclaiming that "Tonight at dinner, every Wikipedian should say a toast to Magnus and his many inventions."<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 January 2002 |title=[Wikipedia-l] Celebration |url=https://lists.wikimedia.org/pipermail/wikipedia-l/2002-January/001164.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031022315/https://lists.wikimedia.org/pipermail/wikipedia-l/2002-January/001164.html |archive-date=31 October 2020 |access-date=4 June 2013}}</ref>

[[Larry Sanger]], in his memoir on the early history of Wikipedia, highlighted the contributions of Manske to the project and attributes the eventual success of Wikipedia to a core group of actors, including Manske:<ref>{{Cite book |last=Larry Sanger |title=Open Sources 2.0: The Continuing Evolution |publisher=O'Reilly Media |year=2008 |isbn=978-0-596-55389-0 |editor-last=Chris DiBona |page=317 |chapter=The Early History of Nupedia and Wikipedia: A Memoir |editor-last2=Danese Cooper |editor-last3=Mark Stone}}</ref>

{{Blockquote
| Wikipedia started with a handful of people, many from Nupedia. The influence of Nupedians was crucial early on. I think, especially, of the tireless Magnus Manske (who worked on the software for both projects), our resident stickler Ruth Ifcher, and the very smart poker-playing programmer [[Lee Daniel Crocker]]—to name a few...Still, because the project started with these good people, and we were able to adopt, explain, and promote good habits and policies to newer people, the Nupedian roots of the project helped to develop a robust, functional and successful community.
}}

Manske, along with others, was recognized as a major contributor to MediaWiki by the [[USENIX]] Advanced Computing Technical Association in 2010 when MediaWiki and the Wikimedia Foundation were honoured with a STUG award (Software Tools User Group).<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 December 2011 |title=STUG award |url=https://www.usenix.org/about/stug.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111115607/https://www.usenix.org/about/stug.html |archive-date=11 January 2012 |access-date=4 June 2013}}</ref>
